policy_title: Introduce a Right to Roam Act for England
stated: Introduce a new Right to Roam Act for England, based on the Scottish model with sensible exceptions, to enable people to access green space close to where they live.

source.quote: Elected Greens will introduce a new Right to Roam Act for England, that would enable people to access green space close to where they live and be a first step to resetting our relationship with the natural world. This would be based on the model in Scotland and include sensible exceptions, such as fields where crops are growing.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly creates a new statutory legal right — a right of public access to land — which is squarely within O9's scope of legal/civil rights, modelled directly on Scotland's Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003.

A right to roam directly restricts landowners' property rights (a listed O10 indicator) while expanding ordinary people's freedom to access land — a genuine, contested liberty effect on both sides that earns a real verdict.

Access to extensive green space is currently a class privilege of large landowners; right-to-roam redistributes that access overwhelmingly to ordinary people, narrowing a meaningful gap in who can enjoy the natural environment.

Shared access to green space has evidence-based links to reduced loneliness, civic participation, and sense of belonging — the Scottish model shows increased outdoor engagement — moving specific O15 indicators non-negligibly.

membership_note: The policy bears on personal liberty (O10, property-rights conflict), inequality (O14, democratising access to land), and community cohesion (O15, belonging and shared use of nature). Environmental indicators (O6) are not materially moved by an access right alone; healthcare (O3) and prosperity (O13) effects are too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
